questions.prompt: A senior ecologist suggests including speculative mitigation measures in a public draft to influence stakeholders. How should you proceed?

options.text: Include speculative measures without labeling them to gain stakeholder support.
Remove all mitigation options to avoid controversy.
Advise that only evidence-based and costed mitigation options be presented, and if speculatives are included, clearly identify them as provisional with further evaluation required.
Let the ecologist decide without review because they are senior.

questions.prompt: When bidding for a large program of ecological monitoring, what documentation most effectively demonstrates your capacity to deliver at scale?

options.text: A one-page statement that you can scale if required.
A copy of your company mission statement.
A list of software licences the firm holds.
A resourcing plan showing personnel, training, equipment, logistics, QA processes and contingency staffing with examples from prior scaled projects.

questions.prompt: A client requests a discounted rate for a long-term monitoring contract but insists on retaining full ownership of the collected data. What is an appropriate negotiation position?

options.text: Offer a volume-based discount while clarifying data ownership, licensing for internal quality control, and any costs for data management or third-party sharing.
Refuse any negotiation and present standard rates only.
Agree to discount and transfer raw data with no restrictions.
Charge higher rates to compensate for perceived loss of data value.

questions.prompt: A field team reports encountering an unfamiliar fauna specimen that may be of regulatory interest. They ask for immediate guidance. What should business operations provide?

options.text: Tell them to continue without recording to avoid delays.
Provide instructions to secure and photograph the specimen, record precise location metadata, preserve samples as appropriate, and notify a nominated technical lead for identification and next steps.
Instruct them to capture the specimen at all costs.
Ask them to wait until they return to the office before taking any action.

questions.prompt: Which approach best supports quality assurance of client-facing monitoring dashboards?

options.text: Publish dashboards immediately and update if users report issues.
Only verify the visual appearance of dashboards before release.
Implement a QA checklist including verification of data feeds, metadata checks, user acceptance testing with a client representative, and scheduled audits.
Restrict dashboard access to internal staff permanently.

questions.prompt: You discover that a delivered proposal included a minor error in estimated travel days that increases cost. What is the appropriate post-award action?

options.text: Absorb the cost silently to avoid client dissatisfaction.
Invoice the client for the additional travel without explanation.
Delay fieldwork until travel costs fall.
Notify the client of the error, propose a revision to the schedule and cost, and offer options to mitigate the increase.

questions.prompt: A competitor claims your firm’s staff lack experience with a particular vegetation classification system. For marketing response, what is the most defensible action?

options.text: Provide documented examples of staff experience using that classification, or clarify training and planned upskilling if gaps exist.
Ignore the claim and continue promotion as planned.
Publish criticism of the competitor without evidence.
Change your marketing materials to avoid mentioning the classification altogether.

questions.prompt: When assembling a post-project lessons-learned report for the management team, which element is most valuable for improving future bids?

options.text: A list of team members who worked on the project.
An analysis of variances between estimated and actual costs and time, causes, and recommended corrective actions for future bids.
A copy of the final invoice.
A summary of client lunch preferences.

questions.prompt: Your firm’s social media team wants to publish a short live video from a field site showing active monitoring. What operational check is essential before approving publication?

options.text: Confirm that lighting conditions are suitable for video.
Ensure the video length is under two minutes.
Verify no sensitive species locations, private property identifiers or client confidentiality issues are visible and obtain necessary permissions from site stakeholders.
Check that the field staff are wearing branded clothing.

questions.prompt: A client wants a single-point-of-contact for all queries during a large multi-disciplinary ecological project. Which criterion is most important when assigning that role?

options.text: Choose the most junior person to develop their skills.
Assign a marketing officer with no project knowledge.
Rotate the contact weekly among all team members.
Select someone with strong client communication skills, understanding of project technical scope, and authority to escalate decisions.

questions.prompt: Your firm uses a CRM to track leads. Which data entry practice most improves the quality of future bids and client targeting?

options.text: Record project requirements, decision timelines, budget indications, stakeholder interests, and previous engagement history.
Enter only client name and contact email.
Store passwords and internal private notes in the CRM for convenience.
Use the CRM only for active contracts, not leads.

questions.prompt: A client requests deliverables in an unfamiliar electronic format that your team has not used. What operational step should you take?

options.text: Refuse and insist on your standard format.
Confirm the specific format requirements, assess internal capabilities, propose a conversion plan including QA, and quote any additional effort.
Provide an untested file in the requested format without QA.
Deliver the files in multiple random formats hoping one will be acceptable.

questions.prompt: A project team wishes to promote a recent success story on your firm’s website that includes biodiversity offsets claimed by the client. What verification should you perform first?

options.text: Trust the client’s claim since they are funding the project.
Publish the story but avoid mentioning offsets.
Verify the offset outcomes against monitoring data and contractual obligations and obtain client permission to publicise verified claims.
Delay publication indefinitely until third-party certification is obtained.

questions.prompt: During a proposal review you notice a key assumption about seasonal timing that, if wrong, could invalidate survey results. What should you do before submitting the bid?

options.text: Leave the assumption in place and hope for the best.
Remove any seasonal consideration to simplify the scope.
Double the bid price to cover unknowns without explaining reasons.
Document the assumption, its evidence base, and include contingency provisions for rescheduling or targeted repeat surveys in the bid.

questions.prompt: A long-term monitoring client requests raw species-level data be published to a public portal. What business operations consideration is primary before agreeing?

options.text: Confirm data ownership, any legal or ethical restrictions (e.g. threatened species location sensitivity), and obtain explicit written consent or apply data anonymisation protocols.
Whether publishing will increase your firm’s social media engagement.
Publish immediately since transparency is beneficial.
Refuse automatically to protect proprietary datasets.

questions.prompt: Your marketing team proposes attending an industry conference to network for future ecological contracts. What metric should you set beforehand to evaluate return on investment?

options.text: Number of business cards collected.
Number of qualified leads with documented contact notes and next-step actions that align with strategic sectors.
Amount spent on catering at the booth.
Number of staff selfies posted from the event.

questions.prompt: A reviewer flags potential plagiarism in a draft marketing case study that quotes a public agency report. What is the correct course of action?

options.text: Ignore the flag and publish the case study quickly.
Delete the case study permanently.
Verify the source, add appropriate citations or paraphrase with attribution, and obtain permission if required before publication.
Replace the quoted material with internal text without checking the original report.

questions.prompt: An important client asks for an expedited project start date before your team has cleared procurement checks with a new subcontractor. What escalation path should you follow?

options.text: Start work immediately with the subcontractor to please the client.
Suggest the client find their own subcontractor.
Proceed without subcontractor and attempt to replicate their capability internally.
Inform the client of procurement requirements, escalate to contracting and the project sponsor to approve an accelerated procurement path or temporary alternative while checks complete.
